## The Path to True Understanding {.passage-heading}

```{=html}
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="1"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p1" title="Paragraph 1 in the full text">1</a></div><div class="note-text">No man shall attain the shores of the ocean of true understanding except he be detached from all that is in heaven and on earth. Sanctify your souls, O ye peoples of the world, that haply ye may attain that station which God hath destined for you and enter thus the tabernacle which, according to the dispensations of Providence, hath been raised in the firmament of the <span class="gl-ref" data-gl="bayan" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: Bayán">Bayán</span>.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 1" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 1…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="2"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p2" title="Paragraph 2 in the full text">2</a></div><div class="note-text">The essence of these words is this: they that tread the path of faith, they that thirst for the wine of certitude, must cleanse themselves of all that is earthly—their ears from idle talk, their minds from vain imaginings, their hearts from worldly affections, their eyes from that which perisheth. They should put their trust in God, and, holding fast unto Him, follow in His way. Then will they be made worthy of the effulgent glories of the sun of divine knowledge and understanding, and become the recipients of a grace that is infinite and unseen, inasmuch as man can never hope to attain unto the knowledge of the All-Glorious, can never quaff from the stream of divine knowledge and wisdom, can never enter the abode of immortality, nor partake of the cup of divine nearness and favor, unless and until he ceases to regard the words and deeds of mortal men as a standard for the true understanding and recognition of God and His Prophets.</div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 2" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 2…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
```

::: {.passage-body}
1. Bahá'u'lláh claims that walking a path of faith requires certain qualities in order to lead the seeker to a true understanding and recognition of God and His Prophets. Specifically we must cleanse our ears, our minds, our hearts and our eyes from earthly things. It may be helpful for you to pause and reflect on what you consider to be earthly. It may assist you to consider the categories that Bahá'u'lláh lays out and think of examples of each:
    1. their ears from idle talk
    2. their minds from vain imaginings
    3. their hearts from worldly affections
    4. their eyes from that which perisheth
2. It may seem strange that Bahá'u'lláh asks the reader at the outset to 'put their trust in God' and 'follow in His way' when the objective of the journey is to understand and recognize God. This seems to imply that the path towards certitude is cyclical rather than linear. What is your understanding of this?
3. Bahá'u'lláh concludes this passage with the idea that 'the words and deeds of mortal men' are not a reliable standard on which to base our 'recognition of God and His Prophets'. You have surely heard people give many reasons for their belief in a particular Manifestation of God. In which of the following has the individual used the words and deeds of mortal men as a standard for the recognition of God or His Prophets?
    1. Upon reaching the age of 15, someone decides to become a Baha'i because their parents are Baha'is
    2. An individual decides to become a Baha'i because a podcast host, who they look up to, is a Baha'i
    2. An individual feels the warmth and love of the Baha'i community and decides to enroll
    3. An individual discerns the signs of disunity and antipathy between members of a Baha'i community and decides to unenroll
    4. After witnessing the transformative impact of the institute process on their neighborhood, an individual appreciates the potency of Bahá'u'lláh's Revelation
    5. After a long period in which the institute process appears to have produced no impact in one's neighborhood, and individual waivers in their belief in the potency of Bahá'u'lláh's Revelation
    6. An individual is struggling to observe a particular Baha'i law. However, since they notice others in the community are struggling with the same law, they feel it is probably okay
    7. An individual tries to apply Bahá'u'lláh's laws and teachings in their own life and feels that it has made them a better person and improved their relationship with others
4. Take a moment to reflect on your own spiritual journey. What is your current attitude towards the claims of Bahá'u'lláh? What are your reasons for those attitudes?
:::


## Reasons for the Denial of the Prophets {.passage-heading}

```{=html}
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="8"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p8" title="Paragraph 8 in the full text">8</a></div><div class="note-text">And now, consider and reflect a moment upon the waywardness of this people. What could have been the reason for such denial and avoidance on their part? What could have induced them to refuse to put off the garment of denial, and to adorn themselves with the robe of acceptance? Moreover, what could have caused the nonfulfillment of the divine promise which led the seekers to reject that which they had accepted? Meditate profoundly, that the secret of things unseen may be revealed unto you, that you may inhale the sweetness of a spiritual and imperishable fragrance, and that you may acknowledge the truth that from time immemorial even unto eternity the Almighty hath tried, and will continue to try, His servants, so that light may be distinguished from darkness, truth from falsehood, right from wrong, guidance from error, happiness from misery, and roses from thorns. Even as He hath revealed: “Do men think when they say ‘We believe’ they shall be let alone and not be put to proof?”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="5" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 5">5</sup></div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 8" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 8…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
<div class="note-row passage-row" data-p="13"><div class="note-main"><div class="note-head"><a class="note-num" href="../read.html#p13" title="Paragraph 13 in the full text">13</a></div><div class="note-text">And now, ponder upon these things. What could have caused such contention and conflict? Why is it that the advent of every true <span class="gl-ref" data-gl="manifestation" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Glossary: Manifestation">Manifestation</span> of God hath been accompanied by such strife and tumult, by such tyranny and upheaval? This notwithstanding the fact that all the Prophets of God, whenever made manifest unto the peoples of the world, have invariably foretold the coming of yet another Prophet after them, and have established such signs as would herald the advent of the future Dispensation. To this the records of all sacred books bear witness. Why then is it that despite the expectation of men in their quest of the Manifestations of Holiness, and in spite of the signs recorded in the sacred books, such acts of violence, of oppression and cruelty, should have been perpetrated in every age and cycle against all the Prophets and chosen Ones of God? Even as He hath revealed: “As oft as an Apostle cometh unto you with that which your souls desire not, ye swell with pride, accusing some of being impostors and slaying others.”<sup class="fn-ref" data-fn="11" role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Footnote 11">11</sup></div></div><aside class="note-side"><textarea class="note-input" rows="2" aria-label="Your note on paragraph 13" placeholder="Your note on paragraph 13…"></textarea><div class="note-bar"><span class="note-saved"></span></div></aside></div>
```

::: {.passage-body}
1. Seven times in these opening passages Bahá'u'lláh asks the reader to 'consider', to 'ponder', or to 'reflect' on the reason for the denial of the Prophets. The more we observe these denials, He claims, the firmer will become our faith in the Cause of God. Below are some extracts which document various reasons people have given for the denial of particular Prophets. What themes can you identify? 
:::


```{=html}
<div class="denial-list">
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"Then said the chiefs of his people who believed not, "We see in thee but a man like ourselves; and we see not who have followed thee except our meanest ones of hasty judgment, nor see we any excellence in you above ourselves: nay, we deem you liars."</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Noah</span><span class="denial-source">Qur'án 11:27</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"They argued, “O Hud! You have not given us any clear proof, and we will never abandon our gods upon your word, nor will we believe in you. All we can say is that some of our gods have possessed you with evil.”"</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Húd</span><span class="denial-source">Qur'án 11:53-54</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"They said, "O Salih! our hopes were fixed on thee till now: forbiddest thou us to worship what our fathers worshipped? Truly we misdoubt the faith to which thou callest us, as suspicious.""</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Ṣáliḥ</span><span class="denial-source">Qur'án 11:62</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"They said, "O Shu’aib! we understand not much of what thou sayest, and we clearly see that thou art powerless among us: were it not for thy family we would have surely stoned thee, nor couldest thou have prevailed against us.""</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Shuʻayb</span><span class="denial-source">Qur'án 11:91</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"The second sign is that He shall rule with a rod of iron, that is, He must act with the sword, but this Messiah has not even a wooden staff."</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Jesus</span><span class="denial-source">ʻAbdu'l‑Bahá</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"And they say: "What sort of a messenger is this, who eats food, and walks through the streets? Why has not an angel been sent down to him to give admonition with him"</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Muḥammad</span><span class="denial-source">Qur'án 25:7</span></figcaption></figure>
<figure class="denial"><blockquote><p>"They called Him a poet, scoffed at the verses of God, and exclaimed saying: “These words of his are but tales of the Ancients!” By this they meant that those words which were spoken by the peoples of old Muḥammad hath compiled and called them the Word of God."</p></blockquote><figcaption><span class="denial-prophet">Muḥammad</span><span class="denial-source">Bahá'u'lláh · Kitáb-i-Íqán ¶234 · <a href="../read.html#p234">Kitáb-i-Íqán ¶234</a></span></figcaption></figure>
</div>
```

[See all seventeen quotations →](../denials.qmd){.more-link}

::: {.passage-body}
2. In your discussions you will probably have touched on the imperfections in the human soul, such as prejudice and closed mindedness that leads to rejection of new ways of thinking and being. Bahá'u'lláh suggests that meditating on the reason for the rejection of the Prophets will lead us to acknowledge the truth that "from time immemorial even unto eternity the Almighty hath tried, and will continue to try, His servants, so that light may be distinguished from darkness, truth from falsehood, right from wrong, guidance from error, happiness from misery, and roses from thorns." What is your current understanding of this truth?
:::
